{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 189,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Data race in search init worker pool",
      "body": "In searchSupport.init, totalBatchesIndexed is incremented inside errgroup.Go closures that run concurrently, and the same closures assign to the outer err variable when calling s.build. Neither variable is protected by a mutex or atomic, so this is a data race. The trace/metric count can be wrong and concurrent writes to err can produce undefined error handling."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 209,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Watch pump cannot be stopped and can panic on closed channel",
      "body": "The event pump started in searchSupport.init receives from events without checking whether the channel is closed and uses context.Background rather than a cancellable server context. If the storage backend closes the event channel during shutdown, the loop receives nil values indefinitely and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent. The goroutine also cannot be stopped by server shutdown."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 203,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Initial index build can miss writes that happen during startup",
      "body": "searchSupport.init builds all indexes first and only then calls storage.WatchWriteEvents. The resource versions returned by build are discarded, so mutations that occur while an index is being built, and before the watch starts, are neither included in the initial build nor replayed from the watch. This can leave the search index stale for affected resources until another mutation happens for that resource."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 88,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized",
      "body": "BuildIndex no longer holds the backend-wide lock during the expensive build, and searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no per-key single-flight. Two concurrent requests for the same missing namespace/resource can both call BuildIndex, duplicate expensive work, and both write b.cache[key], with the last write silently replacing the other index. For file-backed Bleve indexes this may also contend on the same index directory."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 146,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "TotalDocs iterates cache map without locking",
      "body": "TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex mutates the same map under cacheMu. This is a concurrent map read/write race that can panic or return incorrect document counts, especially now that index builds are more concurrent."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 138,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Existing Bleve index is replaced without being closed",
      "body": "BuildIndex stores the newly created index in b.cache[key] without closing any previous index for that key. If a concurrent or repeated build replaces an existing entry, the old Bleve index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and potentially holding directory locks."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 98,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "File-backed BuildIndex may reuse stale documents from previous runs",
      "body": "For file-backed indexes, bleve.New(dir, mapper) opens an existing Bleve directory if present. BuildIndex then writes current documents but never removes documents that no longer exist, for example resources deleted while the process was stopped. Unless the directory is ephemeral, stale/deleted resources can remain searchable after restart."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 263,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Nil IndexMetrics can panic in handleEvent",
      "body": "handleEvent increments and decrements IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other call sites guard for nil. If metrics are not initialized, processing an ADDED or DELETED watch event will panic."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 102,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Nil IndexMetrics can panic in Bleve BuildIndex",
      "body": "BuildIndex increments resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants without checking whether resource.IndexMetrics is nil. Since other code treats IndexMetrics as optional, this can panic during index creation when metrics are not initialized."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 371,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "DocCount error can skip Flush and fail the whole build",
      "body": "index.DocCount is called only for metrics/logging, but its error overwrites err and then prevents index.Flush from running and causes the build to fail. A doc-count failure should not abort index creation or skip flushing; use a separate error variable for DocCount."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 258,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "No cleanup when NewResourceServer initialization fails",
      "body": "NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) and returns immediately on error without calling cancel or Stop. If initialization partially succeeded before the failure, for example lifecycle hooks ran or the search watch started, the constructed server's context and goroutines/resources are leaked."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 925,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is disabled",
      "body": "History and Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can create a server with search disabled, so these gRPC methods will nil-pointer panic instead of returning a not-configured error like Search does."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/server/module_server_test.go",
      "line": 36,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Postgres integration test is skipped",
      "body": "The postgres integration test is now skipped, removing coverage for a supported database path at the same time startup initialization behavior changes. Postgres-specific regressions may go undetected unless this skip is tracked and temporary."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Data race in search init worker pool
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, totalBatchesIndexed is incremented inside errgroup.Go closures that run concurrently, and the same closures assign to the outer err variable when calling s.build. Neither variable is protected by a mutex or atomic, so this is a data race. The trace/metric count can be wrong and concurrent writes to err can produce undefined error handling.

findings.title: Watch pump cannot be stopped and can panic on closed channel
findings.body: The event pump started in searchSupport.init receives from events without checking whether the channel is closed and uses context.Background rather than a cancellable server context. If the storage backend closes the event channel during shutdown, the loop receives nil values indefinitely and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent. The goroutine also cannot be stopped by server shutdown.

findings.title: Initial index build can miss writes that happen during startup
findings.body: searchSupport.init builds all indexes first and only then calls storage.WatchWriteEvents. The resource versions returned by build are discarded, so mutations that occur while an index is being built, and before the watch starts, are neither included in the initial build nor replayed from the watch. This can leave the search index stale for affected resources until another mutation happens for that resource.

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer holds the backend-wide lock during the expensive build, and searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no per-key single-flight. Two concurrent requests for the same missing namespace/resource can both call BuildIndex, duplicate expensive work, and both write b.cache[key], with the last write silently replacing the other index. For file-backed Bleve indexes this may also contend on the same index directory.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache map without locking
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex mutates the same map under cacheMu. This is a concurrent map read/write race that can panic or return incorrect document counts, especially now that index builds are more concurrent.

findings.title: Existing Bleve index is replaced without being closed
findings.body: BuildIndex stores the newly created index in b.cache[key] without closing any previous index for that key. If a concurrent or repeated build replaces an existing entry, the old Bleve index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and potentially holding directory locks.

findings.title: File-backed BuildIndex may reuse stale documents from previous runs
findings.body: For file-backed indexes, bleve.New(dir, mapper) opens an existing Bleve directory if present. BuildIndex then writes current documents but never removes documents that no longer exist, for example resources deleted while the process was stopped. Unless the directory is ephemeral, stale/deleted resources can remain searchable after restart.

findings.title: Nil IndexMetrics can panic in handleEvent
findings.body: handleEvent increments and decrements IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other call sites guard for nil. If metrics are not initialized, processing an ADDED or DELETED watch event will panic.

findings.title: Nil IndexMetrics can panic in Bleve BuildIndex
findings.body: BuildIndex increments resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants without checking whether resource.IndexMetrics is nil. Since other code treats IndexMetrics as optional, this can panic during index creation when metrics are not initialized.

findings.title: DocCount error can skip Flush and fail the whole build
findings.body: index.DocCount is called only for metrics/logging, but its error overwrites err and then prevents index.Flush from running and causes the build to fail. A doc-count failure should not abort index creation or skip flushing; use a separate error variable for DocCount.

findings.title: No cleanup when NewResourceServer initialization fails
findings.body: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) and returns immediately on error without calling cancel or Stop. If initialization partially succeeded before the failure, for example lifecycle hooks ran or the search watch started, the constructed server's context and goroutines/resources are leaked.

findings.title: History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is disabled
findings.body: History and Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can create a server with search disabled, so these gRPC methods will nil-pointer panic instead of returning a not-configured error like Search does.

findings.title: Postgres integration test is skipped
findings.body: The postgres integration test is now skipped, removing coverage for a supported database path at the same time startup initialization behavior changes. Postgres-specific regressions may go undetected unless this skip is tracked and temporary.
